exposure: diagnostic methods (histological features, immunohistochemical results for ALK, molecular confirmation using FISH or Next-generation sequencing)
cohort: Twenty-seven patients diagnosed with uterine inflammatory myofibroblastic tumor (UIMT) from January 1st, 2013 to May 1st, 2023 were included.
finding: Uterine inflammatory myofibroblastic tumor (UIMT) is easily misdiagnosed, and its diagnosis benefits from histological features, immunohistochemical (ALK) and molecular confirmation, with all included patients being disease-free and surviving after a median 8-month follow-up.
